subject: Client SDK compatibility safeguard request
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@olivetech.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@olivetech.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Client SDK compatibility safeguard — ask and matrix

Diego,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. One quick follow-up from our engineering/product teams: OliveTech relies on your client SDKs for our in-app integrations and we need a written compatibility safeguard for the next 12 months of your planned SDK/HTTP API changes.

Specifically we need:
- A 90-day deprecation notice for breaking changes to any published client method or wire format.
- A short-term fallback plan (binary shim or client pin) if a change ships unexpectedly.
- A compatibility matrix that maps Redwood SDK versions to supported runtime/model variants.

I've attached a compatibility matrix template and a short summary of our expectations.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to the 90-day notice and provide a proposed legal/operational addendum we can pin to the contract? If not, what alternative safeguards do you offer to reduce our risk? We're in procurement week next week and this will determine our timeline.

Thanks,

Sarah Kim
Head of Integrations, OliveTech
sarah.kim@olivetech.com
[Attachment: olivetech_compat_matrix.xlsx]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@olivetech.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Client SDK compatibility safeguard — ask and matrix

Sarah —

Appreciate the note and the template. Short answer: we can support a compatibility SLA for customer-facing SDKs with operational guardrails, but we need to scope exactly what counts as a "breaking change" and how the notice is delivered.

Proposal (operational + contractual):
1) Policy: 90-day notice for public SDK surface-breaking changes (method/response signature/wire protocol). Minor non-breaking changes (new optional fields, docs-only updates) would be exempt.
2) Mechanism: Notices via both email + HubSpot deal webhook and an entry in a versioned compatibility page we maintain (we'll share a Drive link).
3) Fallback: For customers on Dedicated/Private, we can provide a pinned runtime + client shim patch for up to one version rollback window (30 days) post-deprecation. For hosted customers, we'll provide a client pin recommendation and a temporary compatibility patch endpoint for major cases.
4) Addendum: We'll draft a short addendum that codifies the SLA and the exceptions (security fixes, force majeure) for inclusion in your SOW.

I'll loop in Marcus (runtime) and Laura (legal/programs) to detail the technical constraints and to draft the addendum. Expect a first-pass draft and a compatibility map by Friday EOD.

Best,

Diego Fernandez
Senior Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com
[Inline: link to Redwood compatibility page will be added]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@olivetech.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Client SDK compatibility safeguard — ask and matrix

Sarah,

Technical notes from runtime: we can produce a mapping that ties SDK versions to runtime/model variants and a small set of compatibility shims.

Couple of constraints to surface now:
- Security/critical hotfixes: these may require immediate server-side changes; in those rare cases, we'll provide automated compatibility shims for 14 days and notify customers — longer support can be negotiated.
- Model variant deprecations: when a model is retired, we guarantee at least 90 days' notice and a recommended migration path; however, older quantization artifacts and custom kernels may limit full feature parity.
- Client pin strategy: we recommend a client-lock file (like package-lock) combined with a server-side routing tag to keep sessions on a compatible runtime for up to 60 days.

I'll attach a short technical appendix to Diego's draft to make the addendum actionable. Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk teams through technical bits.

Regards,
Marcus
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_safeguard_draft.docx]

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@olivetech.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@olivetech.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Client SDK compatibility safeguard — ask and matrix

Diego/Marcus —

Thanks for the speedy response and the clear operational approach. The 90-day notice plus the client pin/server routing recommendation should work for us. We'll need the written addendum attached to the SOW; can your legal team send the first draft (we can redline) by Monday so procurement can move forward?

Also, can you add a short paragraph that commits Redwood to providing automated compatibility shims for security hotfixes for at least 14 calendar days? That helps our risk team.

If you can get the draft and the compatibility map to the Drive link you mentioned, I'll have procurement start the paperwork today.

Best,

Sarah Kim
Head of Integrations, OliveTech
